fields.h1: Build HIPAA Release Forms Patients Can Sign Online
fields.hero_description: Get HIPAA release forms that ask which records go to whom, why, and until when, with every signed copy kept in your database.
fields.features_heading: What Each Field of the Release Covers
fields.features_subheading: The fields follow 45 CFR 164.508, the rule that sets what a valid authorization must contain.
fields.feature_1:
Records listed by type and date range

Patients tick each record type to release, such as lab results or imaging, and enter the dates those records cover. The rule asks for a description that is specific and meaningful.
fields.feature_2:
The sender and the recipient, by name

One field names the provider or plan releasing the records and another names the person or company receiving them. 45 CFR 164.508 lists each as a core element of a valid release.
fields.feature_3:
A purpose, or the patient's own request

Patients say why the records are going out. When the patient starts the release and gives no reason, the rule accepts "at the request of the individual" as the whole purpose.
fields.feature_4:
An end date or an end event

Each release ends on a date the patient picks or at an event tied to its purpose, such as the close of a claim. The app checks that end point before staff send any records out.
fields.feature_5:
Three statements in plain words

The form spells out the right to revoke, whether treatment or benefits can depend on signing, and that records a recipient passes on may lose the Privacy Rule's protection.
fields.feature_6:
Source code you own

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. The release form can then run next to your patient portal, and every later change happens in a repo you control.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Places a Release Gets Signed
fields.tab_content_1:
One release per provider, each naming its sender

Denise Faraday gets one link from Thorne Injury Law and lists her 3 providers. The app writes a release per provider, naming St. Odran Hospital, Cole Valley Imaging, or Sable Creek Urgent Care as the sender and the firm as the recipient. Each gives her personal injury claim as the purpose and ends when the claim closes.
fields.tab_content_2:
Two signatures, one of them for psychotherapy notes

Saltbridge Mutual asks Kettle Pond Counseling for Mira Castellan's visit dates and her psychotherapy notes. The Privacy Rule lets a psychotherapy notes authorization combine only with another of its kind. Mira signs the visit dates release, and the notes open as a second form with its own signature.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each of his two children, until 2027

Arthur Brandvold, a patient at Halberd Family Medicine, names his two adult children on his release: his daughter Elin and his son Johan. He ticks lab results and visit notes and leaves billing unticked. The release ends on Dec 31, 2027, and the front desk sees both names on his record before taking a call about him.
fields.tab_content_4:
When Oscar revokes, the pending request stops

On Oct 6, Oscar Villanueva signs a revocation of the release that let Corrow Point Hospital send his lab results to Pell Street Wellness. Pell Street's request from Oct 9 stops at the records desk. The Oct 2 batch stays on file as sent, since a revocation does not undo what the hospital already did in reliance on the release.

fields.howto_title: How to Create Your HIPAA Release Form
fields.howto_description: These steps turn the release your office uses now into HIPAA release forms that patients sign online and staff can track.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Gather the release you use now
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Describe the form in one prompt
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Paste the statements word for word
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add the signature and the date
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull the release your office hands patients today, plus any version a law firm or insurer has sent you. Note every blank and every statement on each one. That list becomes the set of fields you describe to Emergent in the next step.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write in plain English what a patient fills in, in the order they should see it. Emergent builds the form, the logic that connects its answers and a database table for the signed releases, and you change any part later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Copy in the wording your counsel has approved for the three required statements, exactly as written. Ask for all three to sit above the signature line. A patient then scrolls past each one before the signature box appears.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for a drawn or typed signature and the signing date at the end of the form. Built apps can capture e-signatures; confirm with counsel that an electronic signature meets the law in your state before you rely on one.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Send each release to the records desk
fields.howto_step_5_des: Have every signed release reach the records desk as an email or Slack alert that names the recipient and the end date. Ask for a reminder 30 days before an end date. That gives staff time to offer the patient a renewal.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it with two sample patients
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit the form once as an adult patient and once as a parent signing for a child. Open the database afterward and confirm that both rows hold the signer and every record type that was ticked.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish the form and share the link
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the form on a custom domain, which Emergent includes and charges in credits. Link it from your records request page and your intake emails. Anyone who follows either link reaches the same current version.

faq_plan.q: What is a hipaa release form?
faq_plan.a: It is the signed authorization that lets a covered entity use or disclose a patient's protected health information for a purpose the Privacy Rule does not otherwise permit. Without a valid one, 45 CFR 164.508 bars those uses and disclosures.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a hipaa release form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: the records a patient can release, who sends them, who receives them, why, and when the release ends. Emergent builds the form and a table for every signed copy. Check the result against 45 CFR 164.508 and your counsel's wording before patients use it.

faq_plan.q: Who fills out a HIPAA authorization form?
faq_plan.ref: Who fills out a HIPAA authorization form?

prov.original: Who fills out a HIPAA authorization form?

faq_plan.a: The patient signs and dates it. Someone with authority to act for the patient can sign instead. The rule calls that person a personal representative, and the form must then describe their authority. Add a checkbox for representatives that opens fields for their name and the document behind their authority.

faq_plan.q: Where can I find a free HIPAA medical release form?
faq_plan.ref: Where can I find a free HIPAA medical release form?

prov.original: Where can I find a free HIPAA medical release form?

faq_plan.a: You can build one on Emergent's free tier, which covers building and publishing. Whichever free form you start from, check it for the six core elements and three required statements in 45 CFR 164.508 before a patient signs. An HR team asking an employee for one should send it as its own form, not as a page of the employee information form.

faq_plan.q: How long is a signed release of information form kept?
faq_plan.a: Six years. 45 CFR 164.508 has the covered entity retain each signed authorization as 164.530(j) requires. That section sets six years from the date it was created or last in effect, whichever is later. In an Emergent app, each signed release is stored with its signing date in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Does the patient get a copy of a signed medical records release form?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the covered entity is the one asking for the release. 45 CFR 164.508 then requires it to give the patient a copy of the signed authorization. A records release form built on Emergent can end on a confirmation screen with the signed copy ready to download.

faq_plan.q: Can a clinic refuse treatment if I don't sign a hippa release form?
faq_plan.a: No, outside three exceptions. 45 CFR 164.508 bars a covered entity from conditioning treatment, payment, enrollment, or benefits on a signed authorization. The exceptions are research-related treatment, some health plan enrollment decisions, and care given only to create information for a third party. Collect agreement to the treatment itself on a separate consent form.

faq_plan.q: What makes a hippa authorization form invalid?
faq_plan.a: Any of five defects listed in 45 CFR 164.508. The end date or end event has passed, a core element is left blank, or the covered entity knows the patient revoked it. It also fails if it breaks the combining or conditioning rules, or holds material information the covered entity knows is false. Making every core field required keeps the second defect off your forms.

faq_plan.q: Can a medical authorization form be combined with other paperwork?
faq_plan.a: Only in narrow cases. 45 CFR 164.508 bars combining an authorization with any other document into a compound authorization. Research authorizations can combine with other research permissions, and other authorizations can combine with each other unless one of them conditions care or coverage. That rules out a release sharing one signature with the rest of an intake packet.

faq_plan.q: Can HIPAA consent forms stand in for an authorization?
faq_plan.a: No. Under 45 CFR 164.506, a covered entity may get a patient's consent to use or disclose information for treatment, payment, and health care operations. That consent does not permit any use or disclosure that needs an authorization. A credit card authorization form is a different document again: it covers charges to a card, not health records.

plan.angle: The top 10 is fill-in PDFs from courts, state agencies and hospitals plus explainers (HIPAA Journal, Drata, HIPAA Exams); no form builder ranks. Searchers want to know what a valid release contains and to get one. This page ties each field of the built form to a core element or required statement in 45 CFR 164.508, quoted from the eCFR, and shows four release workflows (per-provider releases at a law firm, psychotherapy notes on their own form, family access with an end date, a revocation at a records desk) where each signed release is a row in a database the practice owns. It gives no legal advice.

claims_to_source: Except where the Privacy Rule otherwise permits or requires it, a covered entity may not use or disclose protected health information without a valid authorization (45 CFR 164.508(a)(1))
A valid authorization must contain at least six core elements (45 CFR 164.508(c)(1))
A valid authorization describes the information in a specific and meaningful fashion (45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)(i))
A valid authorization names the person or class of persons authorized to make the disclosure (45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)(ii))
A valid authorization names the person or class of persons to whom the disclosure may be made (45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)(iii))
A valid authorization describes each purpose; at the request of the individual is enough when the individual starts it and gives no purpose (45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)(iv))
A valid authorization has an expiration date or an expiration event tied to the individual or the purpose (45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)(v))
A valid authorization carries the individual's signature and date, and a personal representative who signs must have their authority described (45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)(vi))
An authorization must state the individual's right to revoke it in writing (45 CFR 164.508(c)(2)(i))
An authorization must state whether treatment, payment, enrollment or eligibility can be conditioned on signing it (45 CFR 164.508(c)(2)(ii))
An authorization must state that information disclosed under it may be redisclosed by the recipient and no longer be protected (45 CFR 164.508(c)(2)(iii))
An authorization must be written in plain language (45 CFR 164.508(c)(3))
A covered entity that seeks an authorization must give the individual a copy of the signed authorization (45 CFR 164.508(c)(4))
An individual may revoke an authorization at any time in writing, except to the extent the covered entity has already acted in reliance on it (45 CFR 164.508(b)(5))
An authorization for psychotherapy notes may be combined only with another authorization for psychotherapy notes (45 CFR 164.508(b)(3)(ii))
An authorization may not be combined with any other document into a compound authorization (45 CFR 164.508(b)(3))
A research authorization may be combined with other written permission for the same or another research study (45 CFR 164.508(b)(3)(i))
Other authorizations may be combined with each other unless the covered entity has conditioned treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits on one of them (45 CFR 164.508(b)(3)(iii))
A covered entity may not condition treatment, payment, enrollment or eligibility for benefits on an authorization, with exceptions (45 CFR 164.508(b)(4))
A provider may condition research-related treatment on an authorization for that research (45 CFR 164.508(b)(4)(i))
A health plan may condition enrollment or eligibility on an authorization requested before enrollment, for eligibility, enrollment or underwriting decisions (45 CFR 164.508(b)(4)(ii))
A covered entity may condition care given solely to create information for a third party on an authorization to disclose it to that third party (45 CFR 164.508(b)(4)(iii))

An authorization is not valid if it has any of five defects: expired, incomplete, known revoked, in breach of the combining or conditioning rules, or known to hold false material information (45 CFR 164.508(b)(2))
A covered entity must document and retain each signed authorization as 45 CFR 164.530(j) requires (45 CFR 164.508(b)(6))
The retention period is six years from creation or from the date last in effect, whichever is later (45 CFR 164.530(j)(2))
A covered entity may obtain consent for treatment, payment and health care operations (45 CFR 164.506(b)(1))
Consent does not permit a use or disclosure for which an authorization is required (45 CFR 164.506(b)(2))

domain_sources.claim: A valid authorization describes each purpose; at the request of the individual is enough when the individual starts it and gives no purpose (45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)(iv))
domain_sources.quote: A description of each purpose of the requested use or disclosure. The statement “at the request of the individual” is a sufficient description of the purpose when an individual initiates the authorization and does not, or elects not to, provide a statement of the purpose.

domain_sources.claim: A valid authorization has an expiration date or an expiration event tied to the individual or the purpose (45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)(v))
